page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture using the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, and AES instructions. This configuration is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and includes 40 GB of local SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the lower tiers. CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, with a Geekbench single-core score of 713.0 and a multi-core score of 1222.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 20.91 GB/sec and write speeds at 16.93 GB/sec. Database operations and web serving throughput are modest, with Redis SET operations achieving 2.52 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 1.77 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and low resource density position this server as a budget-friendly option for non-critical workloads. The trade-off for its low cost is reduced performance stability under sustained loads due to the shared nature of the vCPUs. It is suitable for basic utility tasks, lightweight web serving, development environments, and small-scale testing rather than resource-intensive database hosting or complex data processing.
